Missiles from cargo planes: The new strike idea that could interest India
description: Modern warfare increasingly relies on smart, autonomous weapons designed to disable an adversary’s ability to retaliate. India’s Operation Sindoor in May 2025 reflected this logic, beginning with strikes on terror infrastructure and expanding to Pakistani military assets such as radar sites, airbases and command centres. Even temporary damage to runways or radars can create operational gaps, enabling follow-on strikes. Launch platforms are critical: India fields BrahMos missiles from land, sea and modified Su-30MKIs, while Rafales carry SCALP missiles. To expand salvo capacity, the US developed Rapid Dragon, a palletised missile system for cargo aircraft, now evolving into Dragon Cart. Brazil’s C-390 project with Anduril explores similar concepts. Such systems could complement fighters by turning transports into “missile trucks,” boosting strike volume.

Iyer thanked Laxman for his motivating influence and inspiration to the team.

description: A Delhi man was arrested for masquerading as a Himachal Police officer after he contacted a Gurgaon SHO to restore power to his wife's shop. Presenting himself as SP Chandan Singh, he attempted to exert undue influence. However, the police caught onto his ruse, leading to a case being registered. He later confessed to the impersonation when the power situation was confirmed.

title: Bihar bandh violence: Siwan cop suspended for firing AK-47; 200 NEET protesters detained
description: Advocates allege nearly 200 students were detained after protests demanding the education minister's resignation. Many detainees, including minors, remained in custody for over 24 hours. Police stated 86 protesters were sent to judicial custody and others released on bonds. Violence during protests led to multiple FIRs and arrests across several districts. Several government vehicles were vandalized and police personnel sustained injuries.

title: Jantar Mantar volunteer alleges police picked him up, left him in Mussoorie
description: A man distributing food at Jantar Mantar claims police picked him up Friday night. He alleged being blindfolded and taken to Mussoorie, where he was questioned. An officer reportedly asked about his funding sources and food distribution methods. Junaid stated he returned to Delhi on Saturday after being left in Mussoorie. Police are currently investigating the allegations made by the food distributor.

title: Jeff Bezos ex-wife MacKenzie Scott helped write a 'donation playbook' for Snap founder
description: Snap co-founder Evan Spiegel and Miranda Kerr have donated $550 million to erase medical debt. This significant contribution will benefit over 261,000 Californians facing financial hardship.  The donation follows a model pioneered by MacKenzie Scott, who has given billions to nonprofits.  The funds will be channeled through Undue Medical Debt, a prominent organization.  This initiative targets vulnerable residents, alleviating burdens of unpayable medical bills.
